profile.name: anchor step
profile.tagline: The defining terminating step of West Coast Swing, locking partners in a balanced stretch.
profile.insight: Far from a rigid foot position, the advanced anchor is a shared physical negotiation where partners lean away, balancing at opposite ends of an invisible slot.
profile.profile: The anchor step is the terminating step pattern of nearly all main West Coast Swing dance moves. Together with the slot, it serves as the most distinguishing element of the dance. In its standard form, it consists of three steps danced almost in place with a syncopated 1-and-2 rhythm. Rather than following a strict foot position, advanced dancers establish an away force by placing their center of gravity behind the heel of the forward foot.
profile.profile_long: The anchor step, or anchor, functions as a fundamental dance step located at the very end of a pattern in West Coast Swing. It acts as the terminating step pattern of nearly all main West Coast Swing dance moves and, alongside the slot, forms the most distinguishing element of the dance when compared to other swing styles. In its standard form, the anchor step consists of three steps executed with a syncopated rhythm pattern known as '1-and-2' (or '5-and-6' in 6-beat dance moves) in the general directions of 'back, replace, back (and slightly sideways)' almost in place. The leader executes this with the right, left, and right feet (R-L-R), while the follower uses the left, right, and left feet (L-R-L). At the conclusion of the step, partners settle their weights onto the back foot while maintaining a typical left-to-right (L-to-R) handhold with an active leverage connection. Although beginners are taught the step in a specific way, advanced dancers treat the anchor less as a rigid rhythm or foot position. Instead, both partners place their center of gravity behind the heel of the forward foot on the last two beats of the basic step pattern. They perceive an away force between them, with each person taking individual responsibility for establishing their own anchor. Ultimately, partners settle in this terminal position at opposite ends of the slot, feeling no immediate urge to move in any direction until the next lead commences.

sections.how_it_is_danced: The standard form consists of three steps danced almost in place with a syncopated '1-and-2' rhythm (or '5-and-6' in 6-beat moves). The leader dances R-L-R feet, while the follower dances L-R-L in the general directions of 'back, replace, back (and slightly sideways)'. On the last two beats, both partners place their center of gravity behind the heel of the forward foot and settle their weights on the back foot while maintaining an L-to-R handhold and leverage connection.

episode_brief.logline: Explore the terminating step of West Coast Swing that locks partners in a balanced stretch.
beats: Introduction to the anchor step as the defining terminating pattern in West Coast Swing.
Demonstrating the standard three-step syncopated 1-and-2 rhythm.
Breaking down leader (R-L-R) and follower (L-R-L) footwork directions.
Contrasting beginner foot placements with advanced center-of-gravity shifts behind the heel.
Establishing the L-to-R handhold leverage and mutual away force at opposite ends of the slot.

lesson_ladder.goal: Execute the standard three-step syncopated pattern
